rule.description: Code that a fixed crate-private configuration constant cannot reach in any supported configuration of the crate: a branch or match arm that contradicts the constant's compile-time value, and a crate-internal function whose every reference is confined to such unreachable regions.

checks.description: An `if` guarded directly by a crate-private constant whose fixed value makes one of its blocks unexecutable.
checks.detected_relation: crate-private configuration constant -> guarded if/else block that contradicts the constant's fixed value
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: The guarded block can never execute in any configuration of the crate, yet it is still compiled, read, and maintained as live code.

matches.evidence: `handle_event` guards a resize-reaction block with `if TRACK_WINDOW_DIMS_VIA_GRAPH`, a crate-private `const bool` fixed to `false`; the `then` block (ui.rs:635) can never run.
`push_event` guards an event-batching block with `if EMIT_EVENTS_IMMEDIATELY`, a crate-private `const bool` fixed to `true`; the `else` block (global.rs:79) can never run.
`DepthOrder::update` guards a re-sort-into-retained-index block with `if SORT_ON_EVERY_UPDATE`, a crate-private `const bool` fixed to `true`; the `else` block (depth_order.rs:100) can never run.

checks.description: A `match` arm whose pattern selects a variant that the crate-private constant scrutinee can never hold.
checks.detected_relation: crate-private configuration constant -> match arm naming a variant other than the constant's initializer variant
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: The arm can never be selected, so its retained-state logic is dead while the variant and arm remain part of the code the maintainer must reason about.

matches.evidence: `State::update` matches on the crate-private constant `SCROLL_OFFSET_SOURCE`, whose initializer is `OffsetSource::RecalculateEachUpdate`; the `OffsetSource::RetainPrevious` arm (scroll.rs:241) can therefore never be selected.

checks.description: A non-externally-visible function (private or `pub(crate)`, not a trait impl method, not a test) whose every reference lies inside regions already unreachable under the const-guard relations, or that has no references at all.
checks.detected_relation: crate-internal function -> all references confined to const-guarded unreachable regions
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: Once the unreachable guarded regions are removed, the function loses every caller, so it is dead code that keeps its own maintenance burden alive only through the dead experiment it serves.

matches.evidence: `window_dimensions_from_graph` (ui.rs:1510) is a crate-private free function referenced exactly once, from inside the `TRACK_WINDOW_DIMS_VIA_GRAPH` dead `then` block.

`buffer_event_for_next_update` (global.rs:88) is a private method referenced exactly once, from inside the dead `EMIT_EVENTS_IMMEDIATELY` `else` block of `push_event`, and the `pending_events` buffer it feeds is drained nowhere else.
`merge_into_retained_index` (depth_order.rs:116) is a private method referenced exactly once, from inside the dead `SORT_ON_EVERY_UPDATE` `else` block.
`dims_differ` (utils.rs:297) is a `pub(crate)` helper referenced exactly once, from inside the dead `TRACK_WINDOW_DIMS_VIA_GRAPH` `then` block in `ui.rs`; no other crate code calls it.

excluded: `pub` items and publicly constructible enum variants (for example `widget::line::Pattern` or `widget::text_edit::Drag` in the clean tree) are out of scope: downstream crates can reach them regardless of current internal usage, so the rule never reasons about their reachability.
Trait impl methods and `#[test]`/`#[bench]` functions are out of scope: they are invoked externally (trait dispatch, test harness) independently of the crate's internal call graph.
